chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying: When my community leave it upon each other for the enjoining of the good and the forbidding of the evil, so they would be authorising afflictions from Allah the Exalted'.

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوف: The good, virtuous deeds, or what is socially and religiously recognized as good
key_terms.الْمُنْكَر: The evil, or what is rejected and recognized as bad
key_terms.تَوَاكَلَتِ: They became negligent, left it to each other, or were lazy in performing the duty

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence when the Muslim community neglects enjoining good and forbidding evil?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) links the collective negligence in 'amr bil-ma'ruf wa nahy an al-munkar' directly to the onset of divine affliction, a concept central to Shia eschatology regarding societal decay. This narration underscores that the failure to actively enforce moral accountability is not merely a social lapse but a spiritual cause for God's wrath, reinforcing the duty as a communal obligation (fard kifayah).
